nodes.label: Protected Session Setup (loopguard setup)
nodes.rationale: Setup selects one compatible integration source per agent (plugin when supported in scope, otherwise one fallback), preserves existing settings and unrelated hooks, and is idempotent (repeated setup is a no-op); project scope uses repository-owned fallback hooks when a global plugin cannot honor the boundary.

nodes.label: Explicit Vendor Trust Review
nodes.rationale: LoopGuard never clicks, writes, or bypasses a vendor trust decision; the final setup status before trust is deliberately 'attention_required' so the user must review the exact hook definition and checksum in the vendor UI and grant trust themselves, then verify with loopguard integrations verify.

nodes.label: Attention States
nodes.rationale: Named states (trust_required, hooks_not_discovered, incomplete, probe_failed, daemon unreachable, cloud conditional, setup failed) each map to a concrete next action, and none of them are treated as full protection — honesty over reassurance.

nodes.label: LoopGuard User Daemon Service
nodes.rationale: Owner-only local daemon installed per platform: macOS user LaunchAgent, Linux user systemd unit, Windows current-user scheduled task; Windows automatic startup stays experimental until named-pipe transport and ACL behavior pass the real Windows compatibility matrix.

nodes.label: protected_attached Coverage State
nodes.rationale: The coverage list (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, ...) is exact for the verified vendor/version rather than a generic 'fully protected' claim; controls outside the list remain unavailable or conditional.

nodes.label: DX Report Privacy Model
nodes.rationale: The DX report stores only fixed step names, durations, timestamps, and outcome codes; it excludes paths, repository names, prompts, credentials, and identifiers, and upload is off by default; the feedback command sends nothing automatically.

nodes.label: Uninstall vs Data Purge Separation
nodes.rationale: Uninstall removes the integration but keeps local history; permanent deletion requires a separate 'loopguard data purge --confirm', and purge refuses to orphan an installed service so data cannot be destroyed while a service still writes to it.
